properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 30 at 8:02AM MDT until October 1 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The Eastern San Juan Mountains and the Upper Rio Grande
Valley.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Periods of heavy rainfall associated with a remnant tropical
storm system will spread across southwest Colorado through
Wednesday night.
- Creede, South Fork and Wolf Creek Pass.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 30 at 2:52AM MDT until October 1 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Goodland KS
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of Colorado, including the following areas,
Cheyenne CO, Kit Carson and Yuma, Kansas, including the following
areas, Cheyenne KS, Decatur, Gove, Graham, Greeley, Logan, Norton,
Rawlins, Sheridan, Sherman, Thomas, Wallace and Wichita, and
southwest Nebraska, including the following areas, Dundy, Hitchcock
and Red Willow.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Total rainfall amounts are forecast to be around 1.0-3.0 inches,
with a few areas seeing 4.0-5.0 inches. This is a multi-day
event, the rain will be split across multiple storms/showers.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 29 at 10:07PM MDT until October 1 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of Colorado, including the following areas, Animas
River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, Northwest San Juan
Mountains, Paradox Valley/Lower Dolores River, San Juan River
Basin, Southwest San Juan Mountains and Uncompahgre Plateau and
Dallas Divide and southeast Utah, including the following areas,
Canyonlands/Natural Bridges, La Sal and Abajo Mountains and
Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...Through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Flooding will be possible over burn scars, at low-water
crossings, and along creeks, streams, washes, arroyos and other
flood-prone locations. Creeks and streams may rise out of their
banks. Unpaved roads could become muddy and impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Periods of heavy rainfall, associated with remnant moisture from
Hurricane Polo, are expected to produce numerous showers and
embedded thunderstorms. Heavy rain falling on saturated soils and
burn scars could lead to localized flash flooding and rises on
local rivers. Rainfall is expected to end by late Wednesday, but
rivers may rise out of their banks overnight Wednesday even after
rainfall has ended.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.areaDesc: Northwestern San Juan Mountains; Southwest San Juan Mountains; San Juan River Basin

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 29 at 2:05PM MDT until October 1 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Far southeastern Elbert and southern Lincoln county.

* WHEN...From midnight MDT tonight through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A surge of tropical moisture from the remnants of Hurricane Polo
and a storm system will bring a threat of flooding late tonight
through Thursday morning. Periods of heavy rainfall may lead to
totals of 1 to 2.5 inches in the watch area, with locally higher
amounts possible.
properties.areaDesc: Southeast Elbert County Below 6000 Feet/South Lincoln County
